## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `676d44d593a8e0d8546bac212e2cb335b7aa22ea`

Isolated at-tier contract review of PR #19185 (`Part of #18159`), rendered at 2026-09-19T09:38Z. Inputs: card #18159 and its thread, the PR body / full diff / changeset / check runs, the tree at `origin/main` (`eeaa882459`) and at the head above, `AGENTS.md`, `docs/NORTH-STAR.md`, ADR-0049 / ADR-0066 / ADR-0087, and the sibling `objectui` checkout at the pinned `.objectui-sha` (`53ded82bf7`, 2026-09-05) and at its `main` (`dda8f3815d`, 2026-09-16). Seat comments and the `os-dev-report` JSON were treated as claims, not evidence; every reading below was taken first-hand.

### ① Derived judgments

**The accept-set delta, measured.** My own parse probe (self-tested first: strict refuses nonsense / strict accepts a declared key / loose refuses nothing, 3 of 3) run inside each tree, and the PR's own suite `src/ui/component-record-block-field-security.test.ts` run on the extracted head tree (18 passed, exit 0) and reverse-run unchanged against `origin/main` (9 failed / 9 passed, exit 1: exactly the ACCEPT pins and the three-row census fail, every ABSENCE pin and control passes, so the suite measures the change rather than the tree):

| key | `origin/main` | head `676d44d593` |
|:--|:--|:--|
| `enforceFieldSecurity` | 0 blocks | 3: `record:details`, `record:highlights`, `record:related_list` |
| `redactFields` | 0 blocks | 3: the same three |
| `requiredPermissions` | 1: `record:quick_actions` | 1: unchanged; still REFUSED-BY-NAME on all three blocks |
| nonsense-key control | refused by name on all three | refused by name on all three (strictness kept) |
| `aria` positive control | 21 blocks | 21 blocks |
| `ComponentPropsMap` rows | 48 | 48 |

Every schema is the exported one (`ComponentPropsMap[type] === RecordDetailsProps` etc.), and an absent key stays absent on all three (no default materialises).

**Item by item, against the renderer** (`@object-ui/plugin-detail`, read at the pin and at objectui `main`):

1. **`enforceFieldSecurity: z.boolean().optional()`, no default: shape CORRECT.** All three renderers read `(schema as any).enforceFieldSecurity === true` (`record-details.tsx`, `record-highlights.tsx`, `record-related-list.tsx`, identical at pin and `main`), so "renderer default: off" is what the code does and an explicit `false` is the same as absent to the renderer, which the schema does not pretend otherwise.
2. **`enforceFieldSecurity` describe(): held to the render path, and it does not claim enforcement.** The fold is `useFieldPermissions(objectName).readableFields(names)`, i.e. `checkField(object, field, 'read')` per name. Under `MePermissionsProvider` that reads the server's `/me/permissions` projection (`data.fields[obj.field].readable`, fail-closed while loading); under `PermissionProvider` it reads the client role config (default allow); with no provider mounted `checkField` is `() => true`. In every case the fold can only REMOVE entries, so "never widens access" is literally true. "With it off a denied field still arrives masked or stripped" is the server's doing and is verified in this repo: `plugin-security` `FieldMasker` strips `readable: false` fields from results and masks `maskingRule` fields, with field-level `requiredPermissions` AND-gated into the mask at the ADR-0066 D3 sites in `security-plugin.ts`. `maskingRule` and `requiredPermissions` are live keys on the field schema, so the prescription the text gives ("gate the field itself") names real gates. On `record:related_list` the hook is bound to `schema.objectName`, the RELATED object, as that block's describe() says.
3. **`redactFields: z.array(z.string()).optional()`, no default: shape CORRECT.** All three renderers read `Array.isArray(schema.redactFields)` and test `redact.includes(name)` on machine names; with the key absent the list is empty and everything authored renders, which is the "renderer default" each describe() states.
4. **`redactFields` describe(): held to the render path, and the disclaimer is the load-bearing sentence.** The filter runs in the browser over the block's list after the record or rows are fetched; the payload carries the values regardless. The contrast the text draws is real: the object's `publicSharing.redactFields` is a different key on a different schema, stripped server-side by `plugin-sharing` (`share-link-routes.ts` step 3, `share-link-service.ts` resolving `redactFields` per token). Every one of the six describe() strings says "Presentation only … NOT a data-access control" in the text an author reads. That is the opposite of the failure the North Star names, 「声明即强制,绝不让 AI 声明一个运行时不兑现的能力」: no wording on either key could lead an author to believe it enforces access, and the docs page the drift check flagged (`content/docs/protocol/objectql/security.mdx`) mentions `redactFields` only inside `publicSharing` examples, so it cannot be misread onto this key.
5. **One clause is TRUE on objectui `main` and NOT YET TRUE at the pin, recorded rather than hidden.** `record:related_list.redactFields` says "Applies to the authored `columns` AND to the columns the list derives for itself when none are authored." At objectui `main` the renderer hands the list down (`record-related-list.tsx`: `redactFields={redact.length > 0 ? redact : undefined}`) and `RelatedList.tsx` filters its auto-derived walk by it (objectui#9090, commit `7e50e847ed`, 2026-09-11). At the pinned `53ded82bf7` (2026-09-05) neither exists: with no authored `columns` the derivation ignores the list, and the npm `@object-ui/plugin-detail@17.6.0` this console line last published (2026-08-24) predates it as well; objectui's changeset for it is still unversioned. So the derived-column half of that sentence is not delivered by the console this repo pins today. It is not a FAIL: this file's standing convention is to describe objectui `main` (precedent on the same block: `sections[].hideEmpty`, declared here 2026-08-24 with "renderer default: on" while the pinned renderer had retired the read, restored on objectui `main` 2026-09-16 after the maintainer ruled the protocol correct), and the gap sits on the safe side of the access claim, because the same sentence tells the author the values are in the page either way. Carrier: the next `.objectui-sha` bump past `7e50e847ed` discharges it; worth one line in the card's `Release:` on landing. The TSDoc's "fails closed on an entry it cannot NAME (objectui#9054 / #8793)" is likewise `main`-only (pin: `return n ? allowed.has(n) : true`), but that is a code comment, not shipped describe() text, and the describe() strings make no such claim.
6. **Generated artifacts and docs follow the schema and nothing else moved.** `authorable-surface/ui.json` +6 rows (exactly the six key/block pairs, `authorable-surface.base.json` untouched), `api-surface-declarations/ui.txt` +12 (the three schemas plus their `ComponentPropsMap` mirror), `content/docs/references/ui/component.mdx` +6 rows carrying the describe() text verbatim (AUTO-GEN regenerated, not hand-edited). `react-blocks.ts` needed no edit: all three blocks sit in `REACT_RECORD_BLOCK_ALTERNATIVES`, so no react-tier props surface exists for the keys to reach. The PR's file surface is the dispatched one plus the changeset and the three regenerated artifacts.

### ② Semver level

`.changeset/18159-record-block-field-security-pair.md` declares `"@objectstack/spec": minor` and its body carries `Clause-②: yes (widening)`. Correct by this repo's rules: two new optional keys with no default on three published schemas widen the accept set and remove or rename nothing, so this is a feature widening (`patch` would understate it) and not a break (`major` would overstate it; AGENTS.md: `yes` takes at least `minor`, and only `(narrowing)` is the breaking arm). No ADR-0087 disposition marker is owed because the changeset is not breaking, and the gates agree when run against this head: `check-adr-0087-registration.mjs` prints "this PR adds no declared-breaking changeset (1 non-breaking changeset(s) seen)", exit 0; `check-empty-changeset.mjs` exit 0 (one declaring changeset added, none from the merge base modified); `check-changeset-no-major.mjs` exit 0. Both `Check Changeset` runs on the head are green. The body text that will ship verbatim into `CHANGELOG.md` is accurate to what I measured, including its statement that the third key stays refused.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **`Clause-②: yes (widening)` STANDS.** The governing claim (comment 5740363318) declares `yes`; the PR body and the changeset declare `yes (widening)`. `check-widening-tells.mjs` fed this diff with a hypothetical `no` fires six T1 tells (new keys at `component.zod.ts:1115`, `:1118`, `:1228`, `:1231`, `:1327`, `:1330`), so `yes` is the only truthful declaration, and the arm is `widening` because nothing is narrowed. `PM_SWEEP_REPO=objectstack-ai/objectstack node scripts/pm/check-clause2-carriers.mjs --pair 19185` read exit 0 at 2026-09-19T09:26Z: declaration readable in the fixed spelling, both carriers labelled `needs:contract-review`, pair head `676d44d593`.
- **(a) Leaving `requiredPermissions` refused in this PR is CORRECT.** Verified at the pin: all three renderers evaluate it as `required.every((p) => perms.can(objectName, p as any))`; `can`'s second parameter is `PermissionAction`, this package's closed enum (`create`, `read`, `update`, `delete`, `execute`, `manage`, `configure`, `share`, `export`, `import`, `admin`; `PermissionActionSchema.safeParse('crm.manage').success === false`), not the ADR-0066 capability set the same key names on `action`, `app`, `field` and `bulkAction`. `MePermissionsProvider.check` maps eight spellings and falls through `map[action] ?? 'allowRead'`, so an unmapped capability name passes for any reader who can read the object; `PermissionProvider` routes to `evaluatePermission`, which allows by default when the object has no config (`evaluator.ts:42`). Declaring the key now would ship a parsed security property whose runtime honouring fails open under a shipped provider: the fourth state ADR-0049 prohibits, the "never advertise a capability the runtime doesn't deliver" of Prime Directive #10, and the exact shape this repo's ADR-0087 registry records as "FAIL-OPEN access gates" for `app.areas[].requiredPermissions`. The card's own text leaves the per-key exit to this repo's ruling and the triage grading left it open; the PR's ABSENCE pin is written as tree-scoped, not as a permanent refusal. Stopping was right. Which exit that key takes is deliberately not judged here.
- **(b) `Part of #18159` rather than `Fixes` is CORRECT.** `references/review-checklist.md`: 「`Fixes #N` 仅当合并应当关卡;只落地了可实施的一半 ⇒ 必须 `Part of #N`」 (the source spells the card number with angle brackets, which are kept out of this comment for the sanitizer's sake). One of the three routed keys is undelivered, so merging must not close the card; the body's first section names which half stays open and why. The head's `Part-of PR must not also close its card` check is green.

**Checks on the judged head, read at 2026-09-19T09:38Z:** 39 check runs, all completed, 34 `success`, 5 `skipped`, none failed and none pending. All seven required contexts are green by name: `Lint & Repo Gates` (which carries the spec generated-artifact gates, so the regenerated `authorable-surface`, `api-surface-declarations` and docs are the build's own output), `TypeScript Type Check`, `Test Core` (all six shards), `Dogfood Regression Gate` (all three), `Build Core`, `Temporal Conformance (live PG + MySQL)` and `Governed Surface Queue Guard`. Full green is the landing seat's precondition to re-read at arming time; this verdict rests on ①②③ above.

**Not measured by this review:** the runtime behaviour of either key in a browser (no dogfood run was made), and whether any authored document anywhere writes these keys. The `objectui` renderer was read as source at two commits, not executed.

Implemented-by: `claude/issue-18159-record-block-permission-keys` (mode:subagent, the branch on the governing claim)
Reviewed-by: `session_01JbZnqu8bt6YqfJsr9vaFb3` (mode:subagent: isolated at-tier reviewer, adopted by that seat session)

**VERDICT: PASS**

**Tier, measured rather than taken from the reviewer's word.** Rendered by an isolated at-tier subagent fed only the card, its rulings and this PR — ⛔ never the dispatch order, ⛔ never this seat's conclusions, and told in terms that seat comments and the `os-dev-report` are not evidence. Evidence is the subagent's **own transcript**, parsed per request: **141 of 141** `type:"assistant"` lines stamped `claude-fable-5-1`, against `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` **imported live** from `scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs`; 0 at any other stamp. ⛔ `get_session` was not used.

**`Clause-②: yes (widening)` STANDS** — the review confirms it rather than overturning it: the two keys were refused at parse by `strictObject` and now are not, which is a widening of a published authoring surface.

⭐ The review's substantive finding, recorded because it is the one that matters for this repo's North Star: it read the three objectui renderers, both permission providers and the evaluator at the pinned sha **and** at objectui `main`, and confirms both declared keys are **browser-side filters that can only remove entries**, with all six `describe()` strings saying "Presentation only … NOT a data-access control" — and that the server-side controls the text leans on are real here (`FieldMasker`, field `requiredPermissions`/`maskingRule`, `plugin-sharing` stripping `publicSharing.redactFields`). ⇒ no wording here can lead an author to believe either key enforces access. It also independently verified the **fail-open** reading behind the third key, so leaving `requiredPermissions` refused is correct — and ⛔ it did not rule that key's exit, which is #19186's and the maintainer's.

**One finding it recorded rather than failed, carried here so it is not lost:** `record:related_list.redactFields`'s clause 「AND to the columns the list derives for itself」 is true on objectui `main` (objectui#9090) but **not** at the pinned `53ded82bf7` nor npm `@object-ui/plugin-detail@17.6.0`. Consistent with this file's convention of describing objectui `main` (the `sections[].hideEmpty` precedent) and on the safe side of the access claim. **It is discharged by the next `.objectui-sha` bump past `7e50e847ed`, and it gets a line in this card's `Release:` when this PR lands.**

Every landing precondition is met — PASS of record on this head, both carriers cleared, `check-clause2-carriers --pair 19185` exit 0, and all 39 check runs green at the review's reading. **What is not healthy is the queue path itself.**

Measured this hour on a sibling PR of this seat: #19183 entered the queue at 2026-09-19T09:10Z and was ejected at 2026-09-19T09:27Z with **nothing red anywhere** — because `Lint & Repo Gates` in the merge group takes **28m50s** (it concluded `success` at 2026-09-19T09:39Z) and the queue removed the PR while it still had ~12 minutes to run. Carded as **#19189**.

⇒ Arming now would very likely spend a fleet merge group to reproduce that, and 「合并队列是共享串行资源」. So this seat holds the arm on one **cheap and decisive** test it is already watching: the group formed at 09:27:31Z for another PR is on the same path. **If that group lands, the arm goes on immediately. If it is ejected the same way, #19189 is confirmed with n=2 and this PR waits for it.** ⛔ Nothing else about this PR is outstanding.
